Eight ads, eight arguments

Every ad below is built from one locked vial shot, so the product is identical in all eight. What changes between them is not the background. It is the argument each one makes.

v2. The first pass used a wordmark reconstructed from Axion’s web artwork, and it was wrong: a single horizontal line with the star set off to the left. The real mark is a stacked lockup with the star standing in for the letter I. The master has been rebuilt directly from Axion’s own product photograph rather than from a description of it, and all eight ads re-rendered from that master.

The locked master

One vial, generated once

This shot is generated a single time and passed into every ad as a reference. That is why the cap, the crimp, the brand mark and the label are identical in all eight rather than being redrawn each time and drifting.

It is built from Axion’s own product photograph, not from a written description of the label. A logo described in words gets reconstructed by the model, and a reconstruction is an invention. Copying the real artwork is the only way the lockup comes out right.

The compound area is deliberately blank. No compound name, no dosage, no code. A label that names nothing makes no product claim, and one master then serves every compound instead of locking a separate vial per SKU.

Blank compound area Research use only Matte white, not holographic Copied from the client photo No fine print on the glass

What was checked before these ran

  • Promo code is printed exactly as given. Summer30, not upper-cased. A code is a literal, and an all-caps version is not the code.
  • No imagery implying use in a person. No bodies, no hands on the vial, no needles or administration icons, no clinical treatment setting. Icons count. Checked by looking at every image, not by scanning text.
  • Purity wording sits at or below what Axion already publishes on their own storefront. Nothing was asserted on their behalf.
  • No invented compound names, dosages or codes anywhere in the set.
  • The wordmark is copied, not reconstructed. The master is generated from Axion’s own product photograph, so the stacked lockup, the star in place of the letter I and the faceted diamond come from the real artwork rather than from a written description of it.
  • The tiny bottom line is off the label. Fine print on the glass re-renders soft at ad scale, which is what made the first pass look blurry. Every ad already carries the compliance bar across the bottom of the frame, so nothing was lost by taking it off the vial.

One art direction in the library was built around a hand holding a vial. That breaks the no-bodies rule for this category, and it would have passed every text check. It is now blocked at the source and cannot be picked for any client.
